name: security-mssql-execution-context-review
intent: SQL Server execution context, ownership chains and delegated modules
artifacts: Logins/users, module EXECUTE AS/signatures, ownership chaining, database trust settings and target object.
trace: Follow caller execution into modules and cross-database operations using the actual effective principal and ownership path.
experiment: Use an isolated SQL Server fixture with synthetic tables and two owned principals; compare approved module use and an out-of-policy object access.
disproof: A module that legitimately elevates for a narrowly defined operation is not arbitrary privilege escalation.
repair: Constrain module inputs/context and cross-database delegation, preserving the intended stored operation.
branch_decisions: Resolve EXECUTE AS CALLER/OWNER/principal, ownership chaining, module signing and cross-database trust separately. Permission to execute a module can deliberately delegate its fixed action. Evaluate whether its actual resource/projection violates the caller policy, whether the module is fixed or influenced by lower-trust parameters/editing; do not require editable input before reviewing fixed-module data disclosure.
operational_method: A fixed module can expose forbidden tenant rows even when its inputs and definition cannot be edited; inspect its returned projection and actual caller policy. Separate ordinary ownership chaining from dynamic SQL, which breaks that chain, EXECUTE AS identity substitution and certificate-signing additive permissions. For cross-database access retain trust/signature/user mappings on both databases and whether the module was re-signed after changes. Compare one restricted caller result with the same caller direct-query denial; this may establish intended narrow delegation or an overbroad fixed module.
